deep.reconstruction:
Euler writes ∫1/z^m for ζ(m) = Σ z^{-m}. He writes ∫1/z^m (1/y^n) for the non-strict double sum Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m}(1+2^{-n}+…+z^{-n}), which is ζ*(m,n) with y ≤ z. The '∫' here means summation, not integration.

The problem is to evaluate the double series S(m,n) = Σ_{x,a≥1} 1/(x^m (x+a)^n), which is the strict double zeta value, and to relate it to products ζ(m)ζ(n).

Step 1 (§§6–7, previous page). Use the partial-fraction decomposition
1/(x^m (x+a)^n) = Σ_{k=0}^{m-1} (-1)^k C(n+k-1,k) a^{-n-k} x^{-(m-k)} + (-1)^m Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} C(m+k-1,k) a^{-m-k} (x+a)^{-(n-k)}.
Sum over x, using Σ_x (x+a)^{-j} = ζ(j) − H_a^{(j)}.

Step 2 (§8). Sum over a. The first block gives Σ_k (-1)^k C(n+k-1,k) ζ(n+k) ζ(m-k), the last line of p.147. The second block gives the lines at the top of this page:
(-1)^m Σ_k C(m+k-1,k) [ζ(m+k)ζ(n-k) − ζ*(m+k, n-k)].
The upper sign holds for m even, and that sign is the same for every k.

Step 3. Interchanging m and n gives the other ordering of the double series (the 'right-hand' order of §5). The two strict orderings together exhaust Σ_{x≠y} x^{-m} y^{-n} = ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n).

Step 4. Euler collects the coefficients of the products ζ(m+k)ζ(n-k). One contribution is (-1)^k C(m+k-1,k), from the first block with m and n swapped. The other is (-1)^m C(m+k-1,k). Their sum gives the factors (1±1) for even k and −(1∓1) for odd k in 'Pars prior'. Pars altera is the same with m and n exchanged. Hence
ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) = Pars prior + Pars altera.
Depending on the parities of m and n, half the product terms vanish (next page). This leads to Euler's evaluations of double sums in terms of zeta products, notably when the weight m+n is odd.

The ζ(1) terms (∫1/z) that occur are divergent individually. They cancel formally: the k=m−1 and k=n−1 coefficients are equal and opposite. This is why Euler says the orders are continued only down to ∫1/z.
errors: None on this page. The uniform sign ∓ of the ∫1/z^{m+k}(1/y^{n-k}) terms agrees with the partial-fraction derivation, and so do the (1±1)/(1∓1) coefficients.
The handling of the ∫1/z = ζ(1) terms is formal. They are divergent and only their combination converges; this is legitimate because the coefficients cancel, but it is not justified explicitly.

Neighbouring page (not verified from image): Pars altera on p.149 as transcribed shows alternating signs ∓, ±, ∓, ± on the y-terms. The derivation requires a uniform sign there, so this is either a printing slip or a transcription error. Also, §8 is numbered twice (pp.147 and 149).

ideas.what: Summing partial-fraction decompositions of 1/(x^m (x+a)^n) over x and then over a, to express double series through ζ-values and harmonic partial sums
ideas.modern_name: Partial-fraction method for double zeta values / Euler sums
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Commentarii Acad. Petrop. 20 (1775/1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Expressing ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) as a combination of products ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) and double sums ζ*(m+k,n−k) with binomial coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Euler's decomposition formula (product of zetas into double zetas); stuffle/shuffle-type relations for MZVs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler 1775; modern treatments by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995), Zagier, Hoffman

ideas.what: Formal cancellation of the divergent ζ(1) terms between the two partial-fraction blocks
ideas.modern_name: Regularization of divergent MZVs (formal ζ(1) cancellation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the central computation of E477, Euler's well-known paper on double zeta values. It has been extensively analysed in the multiple-zeta literature (Borwein–Girgensohn, Zagier, Ayoub, Sandifer). Nothing on this page is uncredited or unexplored.
transcription_corrections: Transcription of this page matches the image; the uniform ∓ on all ∫1/z^{m+k}(1/y^{n-k}) terms is correct as printed.
The second-row factor is printed (1 ∓ 1) and the fourth-row factor (1 ∓ 1), as transcribed.
Note that '∫' denotes summation (Euler's summatory sign), not integration.
